all_passages.content: Mixed. I know them as a crypto exchange — solid tech company, regulatory compliant. But expanding to gold is different business model. Do they have expertise in gold custody and jeweller relationship management? That's not a crypto skill.
Then show me who the custodian is on the product page. Prominently. MMTC-PAMP or Brinks — those names are credible. CoinDCX's brand alone doesn't close the trust gap for me.

SGB gives 2.5% fixed yield, gold appreciation, and tax-free gains after 8 years. That's government guaranteed. CoinDCX gives higher yield (5-7%) but with: variable rate risk, counterparty risk, and presumably taxable gains. I'd take CoinDCX if the yield floor is at least 4% guaranteed and there's liquidity. The SGB 8-year lock-in is painful.

Route 2 for me — the returns framing. But I'd want the fine print visible. '5-7%' needs to say 'variable, based on jeweller demand' not just a number. Transparency matters more than the number itself.

Strong product concept. The yield differentiation is real and meaningful. Execute on: full fee transparency, custodian disclosure, minimum guaranteed floor yield, and SEBI-compliant documentation. If you do those things, you'll capture the financially literate segment easily. We want to be convinced, not sold to.
